name: Authorized private food operation gate capability
phase: Specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
objective: Add an independently typed lazy callback gate owned by the existing single-admin service without changing its ten-operation contract or granting reusable authorization.
compatibility: Keep FoodPrivateDraftService unchanged; existing FOOD-001D consumers and fakes remain source-compatible.
Add separate FoodPrivateDraftOperationGate capability implemented on existing SingleAdminFoodDraftService.
Add no new implementation files; preserve existing ten operations, five operation-error codes and authorization semantics.
authorization: Reuse FOOD-001D's existing private authorization logic directly; administrator identity remains injected and canonical.
Resolve authorization fresh on every runAuthorized invocation. No repository call is required merely to authorize; possession of a food ID is never permission.
Never cache an authorization decision, issue reusable permission or authorize once for an entire request.
Preserve unauthenticated, forbidden, unavailable, malformed/noncanonical resolved principal and resolver-failure semantics.
Denied/unavailable callers invoke the callback zero times and cannot learn whether it is callable.
callbackBehavior: Check callability only after authorization succeeds. A noncallable callback then returns fixed callback-failed, with no separate validation vocabulary.
Invoke an authorized callable exactly once with no arguments; support synchronous values and asynchronous callbacks and await completion.
Treat fulfilled callback values as opaque. A returned object such as { ok: false, ... } is a successful callback value nested inside the outer gate success.
Do not reinterpret parser, transport or domain result values as authorization or repository failures.

Catch synchronous throws and asynchronous rejection and return only fixed callback-failed feedback; expose no exception text, stack traces, submitted payloads, private evidence or repository/SQL/D1 details.
Successful opaque values are not transformed into authorization tokens; the callback remains trusted injected code responsible for its own bounded result contract.

resultModel.authorizationFailure: { ok: false, error: { code: 'unauthenticated' | 'forbidden' | 'access-unavailable', message: existing fixed sanitized message } }
resultModel.callbackFailure: { ok: false, error: { code: 'callback-failed', message: 'Private food operation could not be completed.' } }

fixedMessages.callback-failed: Private food operation could not be completed.

resultModel.errorIsolation: callback-failed belongs only to the gate capability; do not add it to FOOD-001D's five existing operation-error codes.

freshMutationAuthorization: An eventual mutation inside or after the callback still invokes a normal FOOD-001D operation, which performs its own fresh authorization.
Never reuse the gate decision for mutation. Honor revocation or caller changes between gate and operation.
No repository bypass, authorization token, role flag or principal argument is supplied to the callback.
tests: Unauthenticated/forbidden/unavailable gates invoke callbacks zero times and make zero repository calls.
Thrown resolver failures and malformed/noncanonical principal resolutions deny with zero callback/repository calls.
Every gate invocation resolves fresh; revocation between consecutive calls is honored without caching.
Synchronous and asynchronous callback successes preserve opaque values and invoke the callback exactly once with zero arguments.
A callback returning an arbitrary nested failure result remains an outer success; preserve its value without reinterpretation.
Synchronous throws and asynchronous rejections return exact sanitized callback-failed results without sensitive information.
Noncallable callbacks are checked only after authorization; denied callers receive only the access failure.
Authorized gate followed by denied mutation performs a second fresh resolution and zero mutation repository calls.
Authorized gate followed by successful mutation performs two distinct authorization resolutions and the normal repository operation.
No reusable token/caching or mutation bypass is introduced; all ten existing FOOD-001D operations and source compatibility remain unchanged.
deferredRuntimeExposure: FOOD-001E/F/G expose narrower FoodPrivateDraftService and remain unchanged.
A later explicitly authorized boundary decides how trusted runtime code obtains FoodPrivateDraftOperationGate.
excludedScope: No FOOD-001J implementation, body/request parsing or Origin/CSRF handling.
No routes/UI, session/runtime changes, D1 changes or migrations.
No commerce/payment, deployment, production data or unrelated subsystem changes.
validationForCurrentTask: git diff --check and new-file whitespace check
currentTaskBoundary: Create only this specification. Do not implement, modify existing files, stage, commit, migrate, configure runtime access or deploy.
nextStep: Review this specification before separately authorizing the two-file FOOD-001D gate extension.
